headings.title: Composer resource discovery and selection flows

html:
Composer resource discovery and selection flows

The @ palette connects text at the caret to existing composer controls. It can search metadata, edit a draft or request a resource link. Task admission and the runtime still own accepted inputs and execution. Start with the UI tour for user controls and the system flow map for the later execution path.

Owners and data movement

mention_palette.js owns one editor's query, listbox, highlight, dismissal and pending selection. mention_cache.js owns shared discovery requests and bounded metadata snapshots across editors and reloads. mentions.py supplies shared namespace/action definitions and the literal grammar. Each mounted palette keeps its own search and selection state. Desktop and mobile shells embed the current server registry; the existing endpoint remains a shared fallback for shells without that bootstrap.

flowchart TD Text[Prompt text and caret] --> Palette[Per-editor mention palette] Registry[Server namespace and literal grammar] --> Palette Palette --> Search[Metadata-only discovery responses] Parameters[Parameter Store metadata] --> Search Context[Context identities and live grants] --> Search Artifacts[Retained artifact metadata] --> Search Search --> Palette Palette --> Targets[Gateway selection owner] Palette --> Ordering[Task dependency owner] Palette --> Modes[Composer mode owner] Palette --> Tokens[Parameter or special-action prompt token] Palette --> Attach[Attachment owner] Attach --> Link[Server resource validation and link] Link --> Draft[Context-reference chips] Targets --> Submit[Later task or instruction admission] Ordering --> Submit Modes --> Submit Tokens --> Submit Draft --> Submit Submit --> Accepted[Accepted execution snapshot]

The main composer delegates attachment state to native_controls.js. Instruction editors use input_resources.js, which keeps drafts by editor scope and includes inherited attachments when counting its 16-source limit. Both provide the palette's attachment callbacks. Gateway and mode changes go through their supplied controllers, and dependency changes go through the supplied task-dependency controller. Their persistence rules are separate from the palette's display state; see composer preference ownership. For editor-scoped drafts, submission retries and saved steering confirmation, see Instruction editor flows.

Registry loading and query recognition

The shell embeds registry_payload() as SMTO_MENTION_REGISTRY, escaping HTML and branding-template delimiters. The palette compiles that grammar synchronously. A missing bootstrap uses GET /api/agent/mentions independently of conversation startup; failed fallback requests can retry. Only speculative metadata warming waits for SMTOReadPriority.ready and the first rendering frame. Mobile mounts resource controls synchronously; prompt-history code and reads load separately.

Recognition requires an @ at the start of text or after whitespace. A selected text range, slash command, quoted code or escaped mention does not open a query. The shared mask replaces literal spans with equal-length spaces, preserving text offsets. Query recognition normalizes horizontal whitespace, rejects more than 256 query characters and chooses the longest matching namespace alias. It retains the original interval so selecting a suggestion does not rewrite unrelated text.

Completed special-action tokens followed by whitespace are prompt content. An instance also remembers parameter/action tokens it inserted and avoids reopening them as the user continues the sentence. Server parameter parsing separately checks the key grammar, 160-character bound and reserved names; it yields tokens without resolving a value. See parameter admission and bindings for that later stage.

Search, caching and obsolete responses

Bare @ shows categories and available mode choices. A query combines local Gateway/task/action/file choices with eligible remote results. Context and artifact search require an existing conversation and remaining attachment capacity. Parameter suggestions can be searched before a conversation exists. Local Gateway and dependency results are capped at 50 each; an already-selected disabled Gateway remains removable.

sequenceDiagram participant Input participant Palette participant Cache as Shared scoped metadata cache participant API as Discovery routes Input->>Palette: Change active query Palette->>Palette: Detach previous view generation Palette->>Cache: Exact snapshot or matching known metadata Cache-->>Palette: Fresh or retained provisional rows Palette-->>Input: Render immediately opt Exact query is missing or stale Palette->>Cache: Revalidate (180 ms typing debounce; immediate category browse) Cache->>API: Coalesced reads per scope, kind and query loop Each category settles independently API-->>Cache: Metadata or category error Cache->>Cache: Fence session and retain successful allowlisted metadata Cache-->>Palette: Notify matching views Palette->>Palette: Check generation, conversation, focus and token Palette-->>Input: Refresh current list, retaining selection identity end end

The shared cache keys snapshots by conversation, resource kind and normalized query. Exact snapshots, including empty results, override provisional matches derived from other queries. Local filtering mirrors the endpoints' searchable metadata fields; it never treats a bounded subset as the complete collection. Requests retain the existing server-side search and result limits.

Snapshots are fresh for 30 seconds and retained for seven days. The cache bounds both memory and storage to 64 query snapshots and a conservative 256 KiB UTF-16 JSON estimate, evicting least-recently-used entries. It hydrates once at startup and writes after rendering, with a page-exit flush. The portal's existing storage wrapper isolates installation, signed-in actor and selected workspace; each snapshot adds conversation scope. Missing account scoping, malformed storage and quota failures fall back to memory. Only allowlisted discovery metadata is stored, including parameter field names but never values, document bodies or execution authority. Sign-out clears the cache and fences/aborts pending reads.

Closing a palette detaches its query without clearing snapshots or aborting shared reads. The active editor's bounded defaults and last query refresh in the background while the page is visible, including while the palette is closed. Parameter changes mark parameter snapshots stale; run/task/chat changes mark context and artifact snapshots stale. Settings changes and transport resynchronization invalidate all kinds. Parameter create/update/delete publishers notify only after successful store operations. Mobile forwards topics through smto:resources-changed. Refresh waves are coalesced to at most one per category per second, with one trailing wave for changes received during a pending read. Hidden pages pause speculative refresh.

A late successful response can populate its original cache scope, but cannot reopen a dismissed view or overwrite another query or conversation. Partial failures keep known results and show category feedback. Selection still validates current resource authority; a 403/404 removes the rejected resource from all snapshots in the scope and fences its reappearance from older pending reads. Gateway and active-task availability remain with their live controllers.

Root results rank exact matches, then prefixes, then other matches, with namespace order breaking ties. Navigation choices precede those ranked resource results.

Discovery route Projection and limits
GET /api/agent/mentions/parameters Query up to 256 characters; default 50, allowed limit 1–1,000. Searches key, normalized key, description, aliases and tags across the collection before applying the limit. Returns metadata and value field names, excluding values. Reserved-name conflicts disable selection.
GET /api/agent/context/sources Requires a live destination conversation; query up to 256 characters, default 20, maximum 50. Lists sources with at least one live conversation grant. Matches identity, name, media type and source kind; excludes file contents and arbitrary provenance fields. Missing body files are filtered after the result limit, so a page may be short.
GET /api/agent/context/artifacts Same conversation/query/result bounds as context discovery. Returns retained result identities, normalized status, completion, capability and bounded field names. Searches reference, capability and field names; excludes values and result bodies. Aliases retain their visible run identity. Missing or tombstoned owners are excluded.

The active Controller reads indexed metadata through memory_context_metadata.py and memory_artifact_metadata.py, using a coherent conversation/native-state view. Parameter search has RAM and standalone SQLite implementations. Its literal, Unicode-lowercased metadata search does not search value field names, even though suggestions display those names. Context/artifact substring matching preserves the standalone SQL ASCII-folding semantics. Discovery does not add a destination grant or fetch attachment bodies.

What selection changes

flowchart TD Choice[Select current enabled row] --> Check{Same query and interactive editor?} Check -->|No| Ignore[Leave draft unchanged] Check -->|Yes| Kind{Choice kind} Kind -->|Category| Namespace[Replace query with namespace prefix] Kind -->|Mode| Mode[Consume query and delegate mode selection] Kind -->|Run After| Dependency[Recheck task and set or clear dependency] Kind -->|Parameter or action| Insert[Insert canonical prompt token plus space] Kind -->|Gateway| Gateway[Toggle through target-selection owner] Kind -->|File| Picker[Open file chooser] Kind -->|Context or artifact| Attach[Await attachment owner] Dependency -->|Accepted| Consume[Consume captured query] Gateway -->|Accepted| Consume Picker --> Consume Attach --> Guard{Attached, same conversation, unlocked and prefix intact?} Guard -->|Yes| Consume Guard -->|No| Retain[Keep current input text] Namespace --> Discover[Refresh category suggestions] Insert --> Draft[Notify draft owner] Mode --> Draft Consume --> Draft

Parameter selection inserts @ plus the canonical mention key; it does not resolve or snapshot the value. Use memory inserts @use_memory. Dependency selection rechecks availability and conversation identity through its owner before consuming the query. Mode selection consumes the query and invokes the mode controller without awaiting its completion. Opening the file chooser consumes @file even if the user later cancels that chooser.

Asynchronous attachment success consumes the captured interval only when the conversation is unchanged, the editor is still interactive and text through that interval retains its original prefix. Text appended after the query is preserved. The attachment owner separately decides whether a returned resource may enter its current draft. A successful server grant can therefore exist even when navigation or a newer editor revision prevents a chip or text update.

Resource linking and authority

sequenceDiagram participant Palette participant Owner as Attachment draft owner participant API as POST context/link participant State as Conversation and native stores participant Context as ContextStore Palette->>Owner: Attach chosen context or artifact Owner->>Owner: Check editor capacity and capture scope/revision Owner->>API: Source identity and target conversation API->>State: Acquire shared queue/deletion lock API->>State: Require both conversations to exist and be live alt Existing context source API->>Context: Require body, validate source binding, link and bind target Context-->>API: Context identity and byte metadata else Retained artifact API->>State: Require run to belong to selected source conversation API->>State: Fetch retained result by run and reference API->>Context: Publish JSON context with artifact provenance Context-->>API: New context metadata end API-->>Owner: Metadata or explicit 400, 403 or 404 Owner->>Owner: Recheck editor scope/revision and capacity Owner-->>Palette: Attached, obsolete or failure Palette->>Palette: Recheck input before consuming the query

native.py serializes the link operation with conversation deletion. Both source and target must be present and not tombstoned. A context link checks the body file and validates source binding under ContextStore.bind rules, then establishes a destination grant and returns its metadata. Discovery only offers already-granted sources. The lower-level binding operation also permits an ungranted source or one marked retained_reusable; otherwise an existing grant to the chosen source conversation is required. The RAM source binding and destination grant share a transaction; standalone SQLite binds the source before inserting the destination separately. An artifact link checks run ownership and the retained reference, then copies the result into a JSON context file with provenance. It does not create an alias granting execution authority. Artifact discovery requires the same conversation journal binding as the link check, excluding missing bindings and runs whose private journals belong elsewhere. Missing resources return 404; wrong artifact scope or unauthorized context reuse returns 403; an incomplete artifact request returns 400.

The main composer's attachment owner rechecks its revision, conversation and steering state after the response. Instruction-editor resources also use an abort signal and editor revision. Neither an aborted HTTP request nor a discarded late response proves that the server rolled back a link already accepted. Admission later validates the selected references under its own rules; see request lifecycle and task coordination.

Keyboard, dismissal and cleanup

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Palette participant Search as Pending metadata request participant Owner as Attachment owner User->>Palette: Escape, blur or composition start Palette->>Palette: Hide panel and clear active option Palette->>Search: Abort and invalidate search generation Note over Palette,Owner: Closing discovery does not itself cancel attachment work opt Parent cancels the palette User->>Palette: cancel() Palette->>Palette: Advance selection generation and clear local busy state end opt Editor is removed User->>Palette: dispose() Palette->>Palette: Abort event listeners, disconnect size observer, remove panel end Search-->>Palette: Late completion Palette->>Palette: Reject obsolete search publication

Up/Down wrap among enabled choices. Enter/Tab select without submitting while the palette handles the key; unmatched root queries with no rows retain ordinary Enter/Tab behavior. Left returns from a namespace to bare @. Home, End, modified keys and IME composition remain input operations. Escape and blur remember the dismissed prefix; focus or a suitable text/selection change can permit reopening. The listbox exposes active and selected option state without moving focus away from the input. Floating instances track input size, viewport changes and scrolling.

cancel() closes discovery and invalidates selection bookkeeping. Attachment cancellation belongs to the parent owner. dispose() additionally removes the instance's listeners, resize observer and panel. It leaves the shared registry and metadata cache available to other editors.

Evidence and limits

The resource discovery scenarios exercise metadata-only responses, search bounds, grants, missing/deleted resources, artifact ownership/aliases and the JavaScript parser/consumption helpers. The collection-search scenarios cover RAM and SQLite parameter search beyond 1,000 entries, literal matching and exclusion of private values. The selected reserved-name, registry-conflict and lexer cases in parameter references check the shared server grammar.

The cache browser scenarios exercise immediate rendering with held responses, reload persistence, account/workspace isolation, sign-out fencing, storage limits/failures and coalesced background updates. Controlled local/cached renders are checked against a 50 ms handler budget; these checks do not measure live-server latency or arbitrary device paint performance.

The shared editor browser scenarios exercise expiry, reopening, unavailable-resource eviction and events arriving during pending discovery at desktop and phone widths. The composer browser scenarios also exercise desktop and mobile update-stream invalidation and attachment flows. These fixtures use temporary storage, mocked transport or a scripted runtime; they do not establish live model/Gateway behavior. The parser Node check alone does not exercise the mounted DOM controller. The related owners are reviewed only at the boundaries described here.
